features.name: any_analogy_counterargument
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment use an analogy to a familiar scenario?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of counter-argument comments by other users. Return 1 if at least one comment itself uses an analogy, i.e. compares the OP's issue to a different, familiar everyday or well-known scenario to make its point (e.g. 'it's like when ...'). Return 0 if no comment does so. Count the commenter's own analogies, not analogies merely quoted from others unless the commenter adopts them. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Literal examples of the OP's own topic are not analogies. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed input gives null.

h0: any_analogy_counterargument has no association with the likelihood of the OP changing their view (delta).
h1: Discussions with any_analogy_counterargument=1 have a higher likelihood of the OP changing their view than those with 0.
note: Operationalized as presence of at least one analogy-using counter-argument comment; "familiar scenarios" is judged by the annotator. OC_comments may contain text after the outcome and no timing is available, so analogy use may follow or reflect the view change. Association only, not causal.
